_about.purpose: The corrected, primer-trimmed run's values for the manuscript, with the results files each comes from and how exactly it reproduces. Built by python/build_results_reference.py from the run of record; no value is typed in by hand.
_about.manuscript: Quantitative Fragility and Ecological Robustness in Machine-Learning-Predicted Chain Elongation: A Multi-Study, Multi-Platform Validation Framework

run_of_record.folder: results/primer_trimmed_2026-10-06 (copied unchanged from the laptop run; see its README)

stage6_folder_of_each_script.03b: not yet run for the run of record

_about.precision: Each value is rounded as the manuscript reports it: R2, Spearman rho, p-values, mean |SHAP| and Bray-Curtis to 3 decimals; RMSE, MAE, concentrations (mM C) and percentages to 1; counts exactly. Values read from a log keep the decimals the log prints.

tolerance.exact: Every model of the corrected pipeline is deterministic. XGBoost runs without row or column subsampling; the few random parts are seeded (07a's LightGBM random-forest mode, 07d's random forest, the 999 shuffles of 03 and of each 03b shuffle, the seeds 0-19 of 07b and 11), and the vessel folds of 04 and 09 break ties by name. With the pinned versions every value reproduces to every decimal given, on any machine: --check on the cloud's own runs of the same scripts (Linux, from its own copy of the matrices) finds no value that differs from the laptop run of record (Windows 11).
tolerance.monte_carlo: The p-values of 03 and 03b reproduce exactly, because every shuffle is seeded, but they are estimates over 999 shuffles; their Monte Carlo standard error is given with them.
tolerance.check: python python/build_results_reference.py --check <your corrected_<date> folder> lists every value of your run that differs from this file by more than half a unit in its last decimal.

_about.earlier_values: The published run's values (before primer trimming, with the earlier settings and predictors) are in this file as it stood at tag draft-v1-2026-10-04 (commit 29635f7). They reproduce with the code at commit 844f478.
_about.sources_note: Paths in each section's _source are relative to results/primer_trimmed_2026-10-06 unless marked as repository paths.

primer_trimming._note: Both primers are cut off every read pair with cutadapt before DADA2, anchored at the start of the read; pairs in which either primer is not found are discarded. The published run kept the primers in the reads. The six scripts R/01a-01f use the same settings (read from them here). The reverse primer is the one some papers call 785R.
primer_trimming._read_pairs_note: From each script's read tracking: pairs in, and pairs in which cutadapt found both primers at the start of the reads (the only pairs DADA2 sees). Brodowski 2022 [Ext.]'s 16 samples include the mock community, removed after DADA2.
primer_trimming._asv_check_note: The same check as R/01a-01f, on the merged and chimera-free ASV table (ASV_Taxonomy_Master.csv): no ASV still carries a primer.

stage2_asv_table._note: R/02 (merge, chimera removal) and R/03 (SILVA v138.1 taxonomy).

r04_matrix._note: R/04 joins the ASV table to the metadata (an inner join), applies data/corrections/ and gives each shared inoculum run one row per reactor it seeded. The runs without a metadata row were not in the published matrix either.

inoculum_rows._note: Left out of every model (data/corrections/descriptive_only_samples.csv); their genus profiles are in inocula_genus_profiles.csv.

prevalence_filter._note: 00: the inoculum rows are left out, the spike-in genera removed, and an ASV is kept if it is present in at least 5% of the modelled Illumina samples, each counted once. Percent of reads: the kept ASVs' share of all reads in those samples (spike-ins removed), from stage4_genus_summary.csv.

final_matrix._note: 00b: the 54 Nanopore rows joined to the 112 modelled Illumina rows on genus columns (an outer join; a genus absent from a platform is 0).

table_1_sample_counts._note: A row is one sample on one reactor and day. An inoculum run that seeded several reactors gives one inoculum row per reactor.

table_2_prevalence._definition: Detected = more than zero reads in a sample of the final 166-row matrix; groups = study groups (of 7) with at least one detection. Mean relative abundance per platform, over all of that platform's samples (Figure 4's definition), and per study group, over all of that group's samples.

Clostridium_sensu_stricto_12.caveat: Not cross-platform comparable: the synonym dictionary (Methods 2.2) maps every Nanopore 'Clostridium' call onto this one clade, while the Illumina data resolve several Clostridium sensu stricto clades.

clostridium_sensu_stricto_clades._note: The Clostridium sensu stricto clades of the final matrix (after the 5% ASV prevalence filter of 00) and the number of each platform's samples in which each is detected (more than zero reads). The clade count is the number of clades detected in at least one of the platform's samples.

replicate_structure._note: Same-day replicates (decision 2026-10-07): in Duber 2025 (Duber_2024) and Prusak 2026 (Hanna_2025) a reactor's samples of one day share that day's chemistry, so they form one sampling unit; every other row is its own unit (pipeline_settings.sampling_units).
replicate_structure._other_note: Duber 2022's bottles: two bottles per trial on day 22 share a trial label but are separate vessels with their own chemistry, so each is its own sampling unit.

rows_sharing_study_reactor_label_and_day._note: The count Methods 2.6 gave for the published matrix (124 of 184 rows; 44 of 104 reactor-days).

table_3a_naive_schemes._note: 10, seed 42 as in the published Table 3a. replicate_sets_split: the same-day replicate sets that the split puts on both sides.
table_3a_naive_schemes._seeds_note: 11: each naive scheme with seeds 0-19, on every sample and with one row per sampling day; median and range of R2.

table_3b_grouped_schemes._vessel_note: 04: GroupKFold by physical reactor (5 folds); ties between vessels with the same number of rows are broken by name, so the folds are the same on every machine.

loso_headline._note: The headline: leave-one-study-out on the full matrix with the core set (Table 4's full-matrix tier 3 is the same number).

loso_benchmark_gain_by_held_out_study._note: RMSE (mM C) of each held-out study under the headline LOSO and under the training-mean benchmark (the mean caproate of the other six studies' rows); gain = benchmark RMSE minus model RMSE, so a positive gain means the model's error was lower. The model RMSEs are 03's observed values; the benchmark RMSEs are computed from the matrix and average to 02's benchmark row.

table_4_substrate_ladder._note: 02: leave-one-study-out, adding predictor tiers, on the full matrix (every study) and on the Illumina studies alone. Only the Illumina-only column adds the compounds measured in the Illumina studies alone (its tiers 3 and 4).

tier_1.description: Tier 1: pH, temperature, HRT, categoricals + genera
Tier 1: pH, temperature, HRT, categoricals + genera

table_5_intrastudy_reactor_transfer._note: Train on one reactor, test on the other reactor of the same study (pairs named in pipeline_settings.REACTOR_PAIRS). The two reactors of every pair ran under different conditions by design (conditions below), so these are not matched-condition transfers. Spearman rho on sampling-unit means.

feed: Defined Synthetic Media / Lactate + Ethanol + Acetate

not_in_table_5.Duber_2022: batch bottles, 2 per condition; no reactor with 3 or more samples
not_in_table_5.Brodowski_2022: CSTR B1 has 1 sample (B2 has 4); the batch bottles are 1 per condition

figure_3_leakage_tightening_progression._note: The same Duber 2025 (Duber_2024) split, B1 (30 samples) -> B2 (21), evaluated with three setups that differ in algorithm and predictor set. No sample changes between stages. Scaling plays no part: 05 run without scaling gives the identical predictions (cloud check, 2026-10-14), since scaling a predictor does not change a tree model's splits. The keys keep their earlier names.

stage_1_unscaled_random_forest._note: 07d, scikit-learn random forest (seeded). Its R2 rounds to 0.155 at three decimals but sits next to the rounding boundary, so it is given to eight.

stage_2_intermediate_unscaled_xgboost._note: 07c: no scaling at all, and its broader predictor list keeps DAY and the alcohols.

stage_3_fully_leakage_controlled._note: 05: XGBoost with the core set (Table 5's Duber 2025 row). Its predictors are scaled on the training rows only, which does not change the result.

permutation_control._note: 03: the headline LOSO refitted 999 times for each shuffle of caproate by sampling day. k = shuffles that do at least as well as the true labels (R2 as high or higher, or RMSE as low or lower); p = (k + 1) / 1000, so 0.001 is the smallest possible. Shuffle i is seeded with i, so both null distributions reproduce exactly; the Monte Carlo standard error is sqrt(p (1 - p) / 999). k and p are recomputed here from every saved shuffle, with the observed R2 at full precision (each held-out study's R2 from its RMSE in 03's table and its measured caproate; the overall R2 is their mean). Until 2026-10-19, 03 compared R2 with the observed value rounded to 3 decimals; the k and p by R2 of 03's table that differ from these are listed in _differs_from_03_table. The 'without' values repeat the test on the mean over the held-out folds other than Duber_2022's, from the same shuffles; Duber_2022's samples stay in the training sets of those folds.
_differs_from_03_table: across studies, Duber_2020: k by R2 307 (p 0.308) here, 305 (p 0.306) in 03's table
within each study, Hanna_2025: k by R2 195 (p 0.196) here, 196 (p 0.197) in 03's table

across_studies._note: Caproate shuffled by sampling day across all studies, as in the published test.

held_out_caproate_spread._note: SD (population) of each study's caproate values (mM C): its own, and the mean over 03's 999 across-study shuffles (the same seeds and sampling units as 03; no model is fitted). A ratio above 1 means the shuffle widens the spread the held-out study is scored against.

within_each_study._note: Caproate shuffled by sampling day within each study, so each study keeps its own values (added 2026-10-11). Each study's sampling units have the same number of rows, so each held-out study keeps its set of values and its k by R2 equals its k by RMSE (checked).

reactor_aware_permutation_control._pending: not yet run for the run of record (no stage6_corrected_* folder with 03b_*.log)

algorithm_selection._note: 07b: XGBoost and LightGBM with the same predictors on three schemes (seed 42), and the two naive schemes with seeds 0-19.

lightgbm_random_forest_07a._note: 07a, LightGBM in random-forest mode (bagging, seeded) on the single 80/20 split at ASV level, with three predictor scopes. The Maximum scope adds the five compounds measured only in the Illumina studies; its attribution is led by caprylate (the target-leakage demonstration of Methods 2.7).

ecological_robustness_claim._definition: 09: each genus's rank by mean |SHAP| in each of 22 folds (7 LOSO, 5 GroupKFold-by-vessel, 10 shuffled 10-fold) on the 166-sample, 205-genus matrix.
ecological_robustness_claim._within_note: Spearman rho of Caproiciproducens relative abundance with measured caproate inside each study, on sampling-unit means. p is Spearman's test, unadjusted and not corrected for autocorrelation between successive days; p_bh_adjusted is the Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p over the 7 studies as one family of tests (not given for the pooled row).

shared_subspace_transfer_control._note: 08 (Table S6): Illumina -> Nanopore transfer restricted to feature scopes, with two guards. Genera as relative abundance over all 205 genera, then subset (or renormalized within the subset).

shared_genera_mean_relative_abundance_pe._note: Each genus shared by the two platforms: mean relative abundance (% of each sample's reads over all 205 genera) over all of each platform's samples, as in Table 2.

replicate_checks._note: 11: how similar same-day replicates are, and the headline and Table 3a with one row per sampling day (each day's replicates averaged) instead of every sample.

figures._note: Values as the figure logs print them (Stage 8, run_figures.py); every input of each figure, with its SHA-256, is listed in its log.

figure_5_top_10_genera._note: One XGBoost fit on all 166 modelled samples, TreeSHAP on the same samples; the top 10 genera by mean |SHAP| (mM C), the Unclassified bin left out.

table_s2._note: 12 ranks every kept ASV by mean |SHAP| in one XGBoost fit on all 112 modelled Illumina samples; 12b builds the table from the BLAST of its FASTA (RID below). A top hit of 99% or more is the closest known relative, not a species identification.
